arxiv-1908-09132.title: Single-pass STEM-EMCD on a zone axis using a patterned aperture: progress in experimental and data treatment methods
arxiv-1908-09132.creator: Thomas Thersleff, Linus Schönström, Cheuk-Wai Tai, Roman Adam, Daniel E. Bürgler, Claus M. Schneider, Shunsuke Muto, Ján Rusz
arxiv-1908-09132.description: Abstract Measuring magnetic moments in ferromagnetic materials with atomic column resolution is theoretically possible using the electron magnetic circular dichroism (EMCD) technique in a (scanning) transmission electron microscope ((S)TEM). However, experimental and data processing hurdles currently hamper the realization of this goal.

arxiv-1909-10702.title: Dimension Estimation Using Autoencoders
arxiv-1909-10702.creator: Nitish Bahadur and Randy Paffenroth
arxiv-1909-10702.description: Abstract Dimension Estimation (DE) and Dimension Reduction (DR) are two closely related topics, but with quite different goals. In DE, one attempts to estimate the intrinsic dimensionality or number of latent variables in a set of measurements of a random vector.

arxiv-1912-06648.title: Fundamental Parameters of ∼ \sim 30,000 M dwarfs in LAMOST DR1 Using Data-driven Spectral Modeling Journal: AJ The Cannon ( Ness et al. 2015 ) , corner ( Foreman-Mackey 2016 ) , matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , numpy ( Oliphant 2006 )
arxiv-1912-06648.creator: Brianna Galgano, Keivan Stassun, Bárbara Rojas-Ayala
arxiv-1912-06648.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Brianna Galgano, Keivan Stassun, Bárbara Rojas-Ayala. M dwarfs are the most common type of star in the Galaxy, and because of their small size are favored targets for searches of Earth-sized transiting exoplanets. Current and upcoming all-sky spectroscopic surveys, such as the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST), offer an opportunity to systematically determine physical properties of many more M dwarfs than has been previously possible.

arxiv-2006-14491.title: Iwasawa theory for quadratic Hilbert modular forms
arxiv-2006-14491.creator: David Loeffler, Sarah Livia Zerbes
arxiv-2006-14491.description: Abstract . We study the Iwasawa main conjecture for quadratic Hilbert modular forms over the p p -cyclotomic tower. Using an Euler system in the cohomology of Siegel modular varieties, we prove the “Kato divisibility” of the Iwasawa main conjecture under certain technical hypotheses.

arxiv-2101-02164.title: A Julia implementation of Algorithm NCL for constrained optimization August 8, 2026
arxiv-2101-02164.creator: Ding Ma 1, Dominique Orban 2, Michael A. Saunders 3
arxiv-2101-02164.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ding Ma 1, Dominique Orban 2, Michael A. Saunders 3. Algorithm NCL is designed for general smooth optimization problems where first and second derivatives are available, including problems whose constraints may not be linearly independent at a solution (i.e., do not satisfy the LICQ). It is equivalent to the LANCELOT augmented Lagrangian method, reformulated as a short sequence of nonlinearly constrained subproblems that can be solved efficiently by IPOPT and KNITRO , with warm starts on each subproblem.

arxiv-2101-05042.title: Analyzing and Mitigating the Impacts of GMD and EMP Events on the Electrical Grid with PowerModelsGMD.jl
arxiv-2101-05042.creator: Adam Mate, Arthur K. Barnes, Russell W. Bent, Eduardo Cotilla-Sanchez
arxiv-2101-05042.description: Abstract Geomagnetic disturbances and E3 high-altitude electromagnetic pulse events pose a substantial threat to the electrical grid by adversely impacting and damaging high-voltage transmission networks and equipment. To evaluate the risks and mitigate the potential effects of these hazards, this work proposes PowerModelsGMD.jl (abbr. PMsGMD).

arxiv-2107-08551.title: A calibration of the Rossby number from asteroseismology Preprint: Enrico Corsaro
arxiv-2107-08551.creator: E. Corsaro, A. Bonanno, S. Mathur, R. A. García, A. R. G. Santos, S. N. Breton, A. Khalatyan
arxiv-2107-08551.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by E. Corsaro, A. Bonanno, S. Mathur, R. A. García, A. R. G. Santos, S. N. Breton, A. Khalatyan. Stellar activity and rotation are tightly related in a dynamo process. Our understanding of this mechanism is mainly limited by our capability of inferring the properties of stellar turbulent convection. In particular, the convective turnover time is a key ingredient through the estimation of the stellar Rossby number, which is the ratio of the rotation period and the convective turnover time.

arxiv-2210-15419.title: Action functional gradient descent algorithm for estimating escape paths in stochastic chemical reaction networks
arxiv-2210-15419.creator: Praful Gagrani 1,2 , Eric Smith 1,3,4,5,6
arxiv-2210-15419.description: Abstract We first derive the Hamilton-Jacobi theory underlying continuous-time Markov processes, and then use the construction to develop a variational algorithm for estimating escape (least improbable or first passage) paths for a generic stochastic chemical reaction network that exhibits multiple fixed points.

arxiv-2305-12215.title: Introduction to Loop Quantum Gravity Rovelli’s lectures on LQG
arxiv-2305-12215.creator: Transcribed by Pietropaolo Frisoni
arxiv-2305-12215.description: Abstract These notes are a transcript of Carlo Rovelli’s lectures on Loop Quantum Gravity, given in Marseille in 2018, which (at present) can be entirely found on YouTube. I transcribed them in LaTeX in early 2020 as an exercise to get ready for my Ph.D. in LQG at Western University.

arxiv-2305-15467.title: (H)airborne: two spinning black holes balanced by their synchronised scalar hair
arxiv-2305-15467.creator: Carlos A. R. Herdeiro, Eugen Radu
arxiv-2305-15467.description: Abstract General Relativity minimally coupled to a massive, free, complex scalar field, is shown to allow asymptotically flat solutions, non-singular on and outside the event horizon, describing two spinning black holes (2sBHs) in equilibrium, with co-axial, aligned angular momenta. The 2sBHs configurations bifurcate from solutions describing dipolar spinning boson stars.

arxiv-2310-19362.title: Floquet non-equilibrium Green’s function and Floquet quantum master equation for electronic transport: The role of electron-electron interactions
arxiv-2310-19362.creator: Vahid Mosallanejad, Yu Wang, Wenjie Dou
arxiv-2310-19362.description: Abstract Non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) and quantum master equation (QME) are two main classes of approaches for electronic transport. We discuss various Floquet variances of these formalisms for transport properties of a quantum dot driven via interaction with an external periodic field. We first derived two versions of the Floquet NEGF.

arxiv-2312-05592.title: Improving reconstructions in nanotomography for homogeneous materials via mathematical optimization †
arxiv-2312-05592.creator: Sebastian Kreuz, Benjamin Apeleo Zubiri ∗ , Silvan Englisch, Sung-Gyu Kang, Rajaprakash Ramachandramoorthy, Erdmann Spiecker, Frauke Liers, and Jan Rolfes ∗
arxiv-2312-05592.description: Abstract . Compressed sensing is an image reconstruction technique to achieve high-quality results from limited amount of data. In order to achieve this, it utilizes prior knowledge about the samples that shall be reconstructed. Focusing on image reconstruction in nanotomography, this work proposes enhancements by including additional problem-specific knowledge.

arxiv-2402-02948.title: Large-scale characterization of Cu 2 O monocrystals via Rydberg excitons
arxiv-2402-02948.creator: Kerwan Morin, Delphine Lagarde, Angélique Gillet, Xavier Marie, Thomas Boulier
arxiv-2402-02948.description: Abstract Rydberg states of excitons can reach microns in size and require extremely pure crystals. We introduce an experimental method for the rapid and spatially-resolved characterization of Rydberg excitons in copper oxide (Cu 2 O) with sub-micron resolution over large zones.

arxiv-2404-01837.title: Rotational mass of anisotropic neutron stars within Rastall gravity
arxiv-2404-01837.creator: M. Lawrence Pattersons, Freddy P. Zen, Hadyan L. Prihadi, Muhammad F. A. R. Sakti
arxiv-2404-01837.description: Abstract Due to rotation, the mass correction of neutron stars arises and causes the rotational mass to be larger than the static mass. In this work, we extend the formulation of the rotational mass of anisotropic neutron stars within Rastall gravity. We apply numerical simulation on the formulation we obtained.

arxiv-2407-17877.title: Advancing 3D Point Cloud Understanding through Deep Transfer Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
arxiv-2407-17877.creator: Shahab Saquib Sohail, Yassine Himeur, Hamza Kheddar, Abbes Amira, Fodil Fadli, Shadi Atalla, Abigail Copiaco, Wathiq Mansoor
arxiv-2407-17877.description: Abstract The 3D point cloud (3DPC) has significantly evolved and benefited from the advance of deep learning (DL). However, the latter faces various issues, including the lack of data or annotated data, the existence of a significant gap between training data and test data, and the requirement for high computational resources.

arxiv-2412-15727.title: Broadband Passive Sonar Track-Before-Detect Using Raw Acoustic Data
arxiv-2412-15727.creator: Daniel Bossér (Student Member IEEE), Magnus Lundberg Nordenvaad, Gustaf Hendeby (Senior Member IEEE), Isaac Skog (Senior Member IEEE)
arxiv-2412-15727.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Daniel Bossér (Student Member IEEE), Magnus Lundberg Nordenvaad, Gustaf Hendeby (Senior Member IEEE), Isaac Skog (Senior Member IEEE). This article concerns the challenge of reliable broadband passive sonar target detection and tracking in complex acoustic environments. Addressing this challenge is becoming increasingly crucial for safeguarding underwater infrastructure, monitoring marine life, and providing defense during seabed warfare.

arxiv-2504-11194.title: Two-Part Forecasting for Time-Shifted Metrics
arxiv-2504-11194.creator: Harrison Katz, Erica Savage, Kai Thomas Brusch
arxiv-2504-11194.description: Abstract Many commercial sectors (such as hospitality) face the challenge of forecasting metrics that span multiple time axes, where the timing of an event’s occurrence is distinct from the timing of its recording or initiation. We present a novel two-part forecasting methodology that addresses this challenge by treating the forecasting process as a time-shift operator.

arxiv-2508-14764.title: Investigation of the Inter-Rater Reliability between Large Language Models and Human Raters in Qualitative Analysis
arxiv-2508-14764.creator: Nikhil Sanjay Borse, Ravishankar Chatta Subramaniam, N. Sanjay Rebello
arxiv-2508-14764.description: Abstract Qualitative analysis is typically limited to small datasets because it is time-intensive. Moreover, a second human rater is required to ensure reliable findings. Artificial intelligence tools may replace human raters if we demonstrate high reliability compared to human ratings. We investigated the inter-rater reliability of state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs), ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-4.5-preview, in rating audio transcripts coded manually.

europmc-pmc10989974.creator: Shen W, Song Z, Zhong X, Huang M, Shen D, Gao P, Qian X, Wang M, He X, Wang T, Li S, Song X.
europmc-pmc10989974.description: In recent decades, with the continuous development of high-throughput sequencing technology, data volume in medical research has increased, at the same time, almost all clinical researchers have their own independent omics data, which provided a better condition for data mining...

pmc-10637045.creator: Hanna Öhlmann, Laura Ricarda Lanters, Nina Theysohn, Jost Langhorst, Harald Engler, Adriane Icenhour, Sigrid Elsenbruch
pmc-10637045.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background and AimsDespite relevance to pain chronicity, disease burden, and treatment, mechanisms of pain perception for different types of acute pain remain incompletely understood in patients with inflammatory bowel disease [IBD]. Building on experimental research across pain modalities, we herein addressed behavioural and neural correlates of visceral versus somatic pain processing in women with quiescent ulcerative colitis [UC] compared to irritable bowel syndrome [IBS] as a patient control group and healthy women [HC].MethodsThresholds for visceral and somatic pain were assessed with rectal

pmc-11510204.title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Enterococci Isolated from Nestlings of Wild Birds Feeding in Supplementary Feeding Stations: The Case of the Canarian Egyptian Vulture
pmc-11510204.creator: Margarita Rosa González-Martín, Alejandro Suárez-Pérez, Alejandro Álamo-Peña, Carmen Valverde Tercedor, Juan Alberto Corbera, María Teresa Tejedor-Junco
pmc-11510204.description: Antimicrobial resistance is a growing concern worldwide, requiring a holistic “One Health” strategy to address the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health. This study focused on Enterococci isolated from Canary Island Egyptian vulture chicks, an endangered species that feeds at supplementary feeding stations in the Canary Islands.

pmc-12434743.title: Association between heat and air pollution (PM2.5 and black carbon) exposure in pregnancy and preterm birth in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12434743.creator: Sreevatsan Raghavan, Tanya Sarah Isaac, Divya Arya, Gabriela Cipriano Flores, Rekha Shanmugam, Ayushi, Bapu Koundinya Desiraju, Vidhya Venugopal, Ramachandran Thiruvengadam, Pallavi Kshetrapal, Nitya Wadhwa, Laura Downey, Jane E Hirst, Shinjini Bhatnagar, Heat in Pregnancy India (HiP- India) Group
pmc-12434743.description: BackgroundPreterm birth (PTB) is a major global health issue, causing substantial newborn morbidity and mortality. Limited literature is available on the association between prenatal exposure to heat and air pollution (particularly, particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5) and black carbon) and the risk of PTB in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This review attempts to integrate existing information.

pmc-13338071.title: Quantum-resistant hybrid encryption framework for secure and intelligent Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication using deep representation learning models
pmc-13338071.creator: Tawfiq Hasanin, Zahyah H Alharbi, Majdy M Eltahir, Radwa Marzouk, Khalid F Alsirhani, Safa Alsafari, Turke Althobaiti, Sultan Almutairi
pmc-13338071.description: Vehicular communications are applied in different security and business applications in the digital world for the user’s advantage. During this, vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication allows clients to exchange necessary information with neighbouring vehicles directly. Generally, vehicles move quickly on the highway instead of the crossing road environment, and therefore, a strong method is needed to communicate securely and efficiently.

pmc-13453943.title: Lymphatic Drainage of Cerebrospinal Fluid Using Lymph Node Seeker 64Cu‐Labeled Gram‐Negative Bacterial Extracellular Vesicles With Positron Emission Tomography (PET)
pmc-13453943.creator: Kyuwan Kim, Changjin Lee, Hayoung Shin, Ran Ji Yoo, Yoori Choi, Chanwoo Lee, Insoo Kim, Jaewook Lee, Minseok Suh, Yun‐Sang Lee, Yong Song Gho, Dong Soo Lee

pmc-13566980.title: Novel Caffeine-Assisted Aqueous Extraction Strategy for Enhanced Solubilization of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons from Creosote-Treated Waste Wood
pmc-13566980.creator: Željka M. Nikolić, Nebojša R. Radović, Aleksandra M. Radulović, Milica P. Marčeta Kaninski, Vladimir M. Nikolić, Dragana Z. Živojinović
pmc-13566980.description: This study evaluates caffeine-assisted aqueous extraction systems for the enhanced extraction of Σ16 US EPA priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) from waste creosote-infused wood. Aqueous solutions of eight water-soluble organic acids were investigated with and without caffeine to assess its effect on PAH extraction.

pmc-13581657.title: Current landscape and research gaps in artificial intelligence for ophthalmic nursing: a scoping review
pmc-13581657.creator: Qiong Song, Xiaofang Huang, Yamin Hu, Kaiqin She
pmc-13581657.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionArtificial intelligence (AI) is advancing rapidly across clinical medicine, yet its application within ophthalmic nursing, spanning emergency triage, perioperative care, day surgery, and patient education, remains poorly characterized. The growing burden of eye disease and the demand for community-based ophthalmic screening create an urgent context for understanding where AI can augment nursing capacity in this field and what barriers may be limiting evidence generation.
